items.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: It was a hot band, very good musicians on it including some from the original Tijuana Brass like the drummer, Nick Ceroli and John Pisano the guitar player.

ctx.x: I see you even did some work with the Tijuana Brass?

I was with Herb Alpert’s re-formed, he re-invented the Tijuana Brass ten years after the big hit. It was the middle 70s and he wanted to come back with a more jazz oriented — he wanted like a Chuck Mangione type approach, kind of a picturesque, macho, flashy jazz approach with a lot of rhythm and a lot of Latin. And it was fun. That was a hot band, very good musicians on it including some from the original Tijuana Brass like the drummer, Nick Ceroli and John Pisano the guitar player. It was a hot band. But it…
I want to ask you about a few of your tunes if you don’t mind. To your knowledge are you the only songwriter who has been commissioned by a baseball team?
